Map: Make the operator app work like Vic.ai (grammar, not skin)
## Destination

DocuBite's authenticated app works the way Vic.ai's does, end to end: **Vic's interaction grammar, DocuBite's skin.** Every operator surface — Invoices, Purchase Orders, Receipts, Bank Statements, Exceptions, Approvals (Invoices / PO Mismatches), Bill Pay, Payment Batches, and Admin — shares one shell: a full-width 62px queue, one header band (View · Sort · summary filter chips opening a hierarchical facet panel), a bulk action row, and one right-hand Detail pane with a sticky bottom action bar. PO mismatches are resolved on the invoice row with per-cell match glyphs and the tolerance arithmetic in view. Payment runs are batched, approved and exported without DocuBite moving money. Admin is a distinct area (Configuration, Approval Flows, Mismatch Flows, Users, Companies) with multi-company access. Approval works on a phone. Implemented and shipped, measured by Impeccable's in-page detector and a critique score above the 20/40 baseline on every queue.

Evidence: the full self-guided tour walked 2026-09-15 — `docs/vic-ai-ux-tour-findings.md` §6 and the screenshots in `docs/vic-ai-tour-2026-09-15/` (DocuBite's own Invoices screen from the same day sits beside them).

## Notes

**Supersedes [Map: Vic.ai-style typed AP surfaces (#177)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/177).** #177's thirty closed decisions are this map's baseline and are cited, not re-decided. Its two open tickets, [Build the five-state processing glyph (#223)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/223) and [Build the typed list-screen composition on all five queues (#225)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/225), are re-parented here. #177 is closed.

**Why a second map.** #177 reached its destination as feature slices bolted onto the old pages, with no ticket owning composition and no in-browser verification, and scored 20/40 ([#224](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/224)). This map charts by *surface*, each ticket owning a whole screen's shape, and every execution ticket closes on detector counts.

**Execution mode.** This map carries execution. Decision tickets resolve first; each spawns an execution ticket; execution tickets close only with `impeccable` run at the four points in CLAUDE.md, in-page detector before/after counts at 1440 and 390 (list and pane-open), and `polish`. Dev-server + seed + headless-Chromium recipe is on #225.

**Design protocol.** Every rendered-surface ticket calls the Skill tool for `impeccable` (sub-command named on the ticket) and `intent`, before the work. Grilling tickets on a surface open with `impeccable critique` of the incumbent and cite the tour screenshot they are matching.

**Vic wins ties, with the tour as the record.** "Does this follow Vic or DocuBite?" defaults to Vic without asking, and the answer is read off `docs/vic-ai-ux-tour-findings.md` §6 and the screenshots — not from memory of the older sections. Grill only what the tour does not settle: DocuBite-only features (Exceptions, Touchless, does-not-move-money, bank statements, institutions), data DocuBite lacks (payment terms, discounts, buyers, entities), and anything that would reverse a #177 decision.

**Documented exceptions to Vic** (decided, do not re-open by "Vic wins ties"): the combined fields+source Detail pane (#179 → #224) with History as its tabs instead of Vic's left panel; the collapsible icon rail instead of Vic's top bar (#224 Q5); DocuBite's palette, type and emerald brand (this map, Q2); Exceptions as its own destination (#192); Touchless keeps its name.

**Settled while charting (grilled 2026-09-15):**

- **Scope is the whole operator app** — queues + Detail pane, Approvals inbox, PO matching in the row, Bill Pay + Payment Batches, Admin, mobile approval. One grammar everywhere.
- **Fidelity is grammar, not skin.** Same layouts, panels, chips, bars, keyboard flow, copy patterns; colour and type stay DocuBite's.
- **Payments never move money.** Bill Pay queue (open bills, terms, countdown, discounted amount over struck-through due) and Payment Batches queue (batch → approve → export file). The transfer stays outside DocuBite, as `preparePaymentRun` does today.
- **Approvals is a destination with two queues**, Invoices and PO Mismatches, each a personal Ready-to-Approve view with the sticky Approve/Reject bar. Exceptions stays separate.
- **Admin adopts Vic's full IA including Companies**: Configuration (per-field Editable/Required/Width, consequence toggles), Approval Flows, PO Mismatch Flows, Users, Companies — one login, many companies, per-entity permissions. This is the one schema-and-auth effort on the map; it is researched before it is grilled.
- **Build order:** shell (#225) → distill (#238) → Approvals → PO matching → Payments → Admin → Mobile.
- **Removal protocol (owner's rule, #237):** nothing is removed from the app without the owner signing off each removal by name on the ticket. Removed features are *unplugged* (CONTEXT.md term), not deleted, so a return is a re-link.

## Decisions so far

<!-- one line per closed ticket -->
- #230 (research): Workspace is already the Company (71/80 models keyed on workspaceId, one Bigcapital org per workspace, nothing above it); one login/many companies already works via per-workspace `WorkspaceMember.role`, the grouping is what is missing; both isolation layers key on `workspace_id`, so Companies should be an additive `Organization` + nullable `Workspace.organizationId` + `OrganizationMember`, with `WorkspaceMember` the only grant of entity access — [docs/research/multi-company-access.md](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/blob/research/multi-company-access/docs/research/multi-company-access.md); eight open decisions handed to #231.

- [Build the typed list-screen composition on all five queues (#225)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/225) (task, shipped): the Queue screen is live on Invoices / POs / Receipts / Bank Statements / Exceptions — full-width 62px queue, one header band with facet chips, 60% right Detail pane with ↑/↓/Esc + sticky Approve/Reject, 56px icon rail, deep links; aging totals moved to the Dashboard as "Open invoices by age". In-page detector Invoices 30/26 · 41/34 → 6/5 · 6/5; critique 20/40 → 25/40. Critique findings with a decision became [#233](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/233) (one status vocabulary), [#234](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/234) (pane header stack), [#235](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/235) (below-md rendering — reopens a #224 choice, loop budget 1 of 2); the leading-glyph finding went to #223.

- [Shape the Approvals destination: Ready-to-Approve queues for Invoices and PO Mismatches (#227)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/227) (grilling): a row is a *submitted* Approval at a stage, never a workflow-less ReviewTask; "me" = `canDecideStage`, surfaced as the personal system view Ready to Approve via #180's `scopeToCurrentUser`; PO Mismatches rows are blocked `match-variance` gates approved by `overrideGate(reason)`; ineligible rows (hard check, open Exception) stay visible and undecidable; same pane opening on Approval with read-only fields and a sticky Reject · Approve footer; Start from the Invoices bulk bar; decisions are Server-confirmed with no optimistic removal or Undo and no single-key approve; approval never publishes; incumbent critique 21/40, in-page 12/6 · 17/9. Execution: [#236](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/236). Glossary gained Approval, Approver, Ready to Approve, Send back for review, Not eligible.
- [Build the Approvals destination: Ready to Approve and PO Mismatches queues on the queue shell (#236)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/236) (task, shipped `b137c01`): `/approvals/invoices` and `/approvals/po-mismatches` live on the #225 Queue-screen shell with deep links; `/review*` 308-redirects there; `review-inbox.tsx`/`review-task-detail.tsx` deleted. New `models/approvals.ts` (actor-scoped, deduped Ready-to-Approve count for the rail badge), `lib/approvals/row-eligibility.ts`, `startApprovalOnInvoice`/`sendReviewTaskBackForReview`/`cancelApprovalOnDocument`; `SplitPane` gained `initialTab`/`fieldsReadOnly` (locks fields while any stage is pending, in every Detail pane). All 16 of #227's decisions implemented as stated, including the full state-10 inventory and no optimistic removal/Undo. Verified: clean `tsc`, clean full-repo `eslint` on touched files, 2563/2563 tests (31 new), successful `next build` with all new routes in the manifest. **Gaps flagged:** `craft-floor.md` (referenced by this ticket and CLAUDE.md) doesn't exist anywhere in the repo's history; `impeccable`/`intent` still absent from the toolset (10th confirmation); mobile stays content-only pending #232; no live Postgres in this sandbox.
- [Decide what the operator app drops or folds to match the Vic grammar — starting with the Dashboard (#237)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/237) (grilling): the workspace home is the Invoices queue on desktop and phone, no overview surface; the Dashboard's nine blocks are dropped (old page behind `DASHBOARD_LANDING` for one release), aging goes to #229 as Bill Pay's metric, KPIs and charts are removed and reporting is out of scope; rail loses Dashboard and the "Review" item, Controls/Close/Health/Activity wait for #231; Worksheets, Expenses and Dictation are **unplugged** at the owner's call (no nav, no actions, no badges, routes closed, code kept). Execution: [#238](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/238); follow-on journey map: [#239](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/239).
- [Build the distilled operator shell: land on Invoices, drop the Dashboard, unplug Worksheets / Expenses / Dictation (#238)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/238) (task, shipped `f99c8ac`): `/workspaces/<id>` lands on the Invoices queue; the old Dashboard survives one release at `/dashboard` behind `DASHBOARD_LANDING`; rail is Invoices · POs │ Receipts · Bank Statements │ Exceptions · Controls · Finance · Archive; phone tabs Invoices · Exceptions · Finance-or-Archive · Settings; Worksheets/Expenses/Dictation unplugged via `lib/unplugged` (four routes 404 in-shell, tested; code kept); a workspace not-found boundary keeps the rail on every dead address. Invoices landing in-page detector 7/5 → 7/5; incumbent Dashboard critique 20/40 archived; `evaluate` 74/100. H6 (11 rail stops) waits on #231; H7 and H10 graduated to [#240](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/240) (keyboard accelerators) and [#241](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/241) (first-run help after the Dashboard); the incumbent's 20/40 and its one good idea go to [#242](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/242).

- [Chart the operator's working day end to end (#239)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/239) (grilling): three lanes (Reviewer · Approver · Owner) across intake → queues → blocked → approve → ledger/pay → lookup → done → Close, in [`docs/journeys/operator-working-day.md`](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/blob/codex/post-login-ux-implementation/docs/journeys/operator-working-day.md); intake has no entry point after #238 (P0); after a decision the operator stays on the row; the Checks tab owns resolution and Exceptions is the list; Finance is off the daily route; the empty queue is "done"; the phone is the Approver's lane; Archive is a lookup side-path; Reviewer order Invoices → POs → Receipts → Bank Statements → Exceptions. Hand-off critiques Exceptions 24/40 · Finance 14/40 · Archive 17/40. Seams: [#243](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/243) intake, [#244](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/244) way back, [#245](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/245) Archive, [#246](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/246) Approver notification, [#247](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/247) expense claim, [#248](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/248) Finance's shape; execution on [#249](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/249).
- [Shape PO mismatch resolution inside the invoice row (#228)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/228) (grilling): #206's best-line assignment becomes the visible View PO row on the Details tab's line items, with `=`/`≠` per cell (quantity by cumulative rule, unit price within the match-variance percent, description as the line match; Total carries the `match-variance` gate; `=` only while View PO is on); line status is a Check status (#233's words) plus Not matched; breakdown is sentence-first then Ordered · Already invoiced (named) · This invoice · Allowance · Over by from structured check `detail`; a Purchase Orders column on Invoices carries the PO chip and a count equal to the `≠` glyphs the pane will show, plus a dashed suggested chip for a likely PO that compares nothing until confirmed; **Match manually** (confirm/replace/reject the PO, `lineAssignments` on `DocumentMatch`, auto send-back under a running Approval, no reason) is distinct from Override Mode (reason); PO queue is Supplier · PO # · Amount · Invoiced · Open/Fully invoiced · Received with consumption in its pane. Glossary: Line match, Match manually, Override Mode, Fully invoiced. Execution: [#250](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/250).
- [Shape payment runs that never move money: Bill Pay queue and Payment Batches (#229)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/229) (grilling, autopilot): `payment_runs` becomes the **Payment batch** (additive columns) with Pending approval → Approved → Paid, Rejected with a reason, and "file downloaded" as a fact not a state; member submits, owner decides, downloads and marks paid; **Pay From** is a named Payer account (new additive model, Settings › Payments) and one batch = one account = one currency = one file; Supplier gains early-payment discount percent + days beside its net terms, shown as "2/10 net 30", and #188's purple *Expires in N days* now has real data; **Mark as paid** writes a DocuBite-side Payment record and paid state is derived ledger-first ([ADR 0001](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/blob/codex/post-login-ux-implementation/docs/adr/0001-paid-state-derived-from-ledger-then-payment-records.md)); Bill Pay lists only Approved, unpaid invoices (the #239 gate), shows bank-less rows as undecidable, and carries *Open invoices by age* as its one metric; Payment Batches has Pending approval · Approved · Paid views and Early Payment Savings only once a discount exists; one rail item **Payments** with two queues, the Invoices bulk-bar "Prepare payment run" moves there. Glossary: Bill Pay, Payment batch, Payer account, Payment terms, Payment record. Execution: [#251](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/251); #248 now also waits on #251.

- [Shape the Admin area: Configuration, Approval Flows, Mismatch Flows, Users, Companies (#231)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/231) (grilling, autopilot; incumbent Settings+Controls critique 23/40): **Workspace is the Company**, Organization is additive above it and never grants entity access ([ADR 0002](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/blob/codex/post-login-ux-implementation/docs/adr/0002-organization-above-workspace-workspace-is-the-company.md)); two minimal role axes (org `admin|member`, entity `owner|reviewer|member` unchanged); one rail item **Admin** at the bottom, Controls leaves the spine and folds in; Vic's two groups — Organization (Dashboard at ≥2 companies · Companies · Users) and ‹Company› (Configuration · Approval Flows · PO Mismatch Flows · Suppliers · Integrations); the per-type field table drives the Detail pane *and* each queue's system-view default columns; Default approval flow (off by default) and a mismatch approver with tolerances; Users and Companies on the Queue-screen shell; Controls' Panel/Ledger grammar is the admin grammar, left nav not tabs, explicit Save on a sticky bar; "Jurisdiction" → Tax; Security and Reset tour move to the account menu; Admin is desktop-only, the phone's 4th tab becomes Account. Glossary: Company, Organization, Admin, Configuration. Execution: [#252](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/252) shell + Configuration → [#253](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/253) Flows, [#254](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/254) Organization/Users (waits on [#255](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/255) scope-guard gap); owner sign-off on unplugging Settings › Templates and › Reports: [#256](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/256).

- [Shape mobile approval against the tour's app screens (#232)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/232) (grilling, autopilot; incumbent evidence cited from #227's 21/40 · 12/6 · 17/9, not re-run): landing stays the Invoices queue on every width, Vic's two-card home is not adopted; phone tab bar becomes **Approvals · Invoices · Exceptions · Account** (Finance/Archive and the other queues as a read-only list on Account; Invoices loses its badge); Ready to Approve on the phone is one list with a segmented Invoices (n) · PO Mismatches (n) control, a Filter bottom sheet and ≥64px cards, no bulk; the below-`lg` Detail pane *is* the phone screen (source strip over Approval · Details · Checks · History; "Approval Context" is now an _Avoid_ term), one timeline component on both widths with avatars, "From this supplier" from existing Supplier data + the near-duplicate check; sticky Reject · Approve bar above the tab bar, Server-confirmed, stay on the row after deciding, pushState so the system Back closes the sheet; full phone state inventory. Execution: [#257](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/257) (blocked by #236); input posted to #235.
- [Decide one status vocabulary for the Detail pane (#233)](https://github.com/petrose99/Wes-doc/issues/233) (grilling, autopilot; incumbent critique 25/40 with H1 = 2 cited, not re-run): CONTEXT.md's five Processing-state words are the only vocabulary for where a document stands, derived once via `processingState()` + one label map on every surface; *Unreviewed / Reviewed / signed off / awaiting approval* and the raw status strings are retired (an untouched document is In review); the pane's separate pill is replaced by a **Status line** (state pill + the fact behind it, from the audit log, Vic's summary-strip shape); the stepper survives but speaks the same words; the Approval tab is never empty on an Approved document — a workflow-less approve shows *Reviewed and approved by ‹actor› · ‹date›* from `document_reviewed`, Touchless its own fact, In review an honest next action; facets become Processing state + Ledger groups. Glossary: Processing state sharpened, Status line. Execution: [#258](https://github.com/petrose99/Wes-doc/issues/258) (blocked by #234).
- [Decide the Detail pane's header stack and where Delete lives (#234)](https://github.com/petrose99/Wes-doc/issues/234) (grilling, autopilot; incumbent critique 25/40 with H3 = 3, H8 = 2 cited; live-measured 192px of chrome above the source at 1440, 143 at 390): the embedded document header folds into **one pane header** — row name · 1 of N · ↑↓ · ⋯ · × over the Status line — and the stepper is the single band beneath it (one line, current node + n of N, below `lg`); the filename and the split toggle move to a **source strip** (Vic's toolbar shape); **Delete, Archive and Flag leave the header for the ⋯** (Delete last, red, behind the confirm; bulk-bar Delete stays as in Vic), the type chip and review-task link retire, the ledger mark follows the Status line; `?full=1` renders the same pane frame at full width, so there is one header. Budget ≤ 96px of pane chrome. Glossary: Detail pane sharpened. Execution: [#259](https://github.com/petrose99/Wes-doc/issues/259) (blocks #258); owner sign-off to unplug the Flag: [#260](https://github.com/petrose99/Wes-doc/issues/260).
- [Decide the queue's below-md rendering: horizontal scroller (#187/#224) or a two-line card row + Filters (n) button (#235)](https://github.com/petrose99/Wes-doc/issues/235) (grilling, autopilot; incumbent critique P2 "clipped desktop table" and #225's 390 counts 6/5 · 6/5 cited, not re-run): **card rows on every queue below `md`, the `min-w-[720px]` scroller is retired** (tour §6 #13, #232's Approvals card; **loop budget 1 of 2 spent** reopening the #224/#187 carry-over); `md`–`lg` hides low-priority columns instead of scrolling; one `Filters · n` button opens the shared Sort-and-filter bottom sheet (Cancel / Apply); View stays as a compact select, stat hidden `<md`, no selection below `md`; one card with four slots (title · trailing · subtitle · pill) declared per queue via a column `phone` role; `ul`/`li` semantics, ≥48px targets; filtered-empty gains an inline Clear filters everywhere. Glossary: Queue screen sharpened (_Avoid_ mobile table, horizontal scroller). Execution: [#261](https://github.com/petrose99/Wes-doc/issues/261), blocked by #257.
- [Decide keyboard accelerators across the operator app: jumping between queues and rows (#240)](https://github.com/petrose99/Wes-doc/issues/240) (grilling, autopilot; incumbent measured live 2026-09-16: 28 Tabs to the first row at 1440, no key does anything with the pane closed, ⌘K `GlobalSearch` unmounted, in-page 3/4 · 3/3): desktop-only set for the Reviewer; **rows are a roving-tabindex group** (Tab in once, ↑/↓ Home/End, Enter opens — focus-scoped, not a shortcut, always on) and the pane's ↑/↓/Esc stays; **`g` + letter jumps queues** (i p r b e a y d, registered from the rail so unbuilt destinations have no key), `f` focuses the facet chips, `?` opens one Keyboard shortcuts dialog (also on the account menu; rail tooltips carry the sequence); WCAG 2.1.4 met by a per-user **off switch** (on by default, localStorage) that disables the letter keys only; **no key acts on data**; no search key — ⌘K revival goes to #245; Ctrl/Alt+digit rejected (browser tabs). Glossary: Keyboard shortcut. Execution: [#262](https://github.com/petrose99/Wes-doc/issues/262); inputs posted to #245 and #261.
- [Decide where first-run help lives now that the workspace home is the Invoices queue (#241)](https://github.com/petrose99/Wes-doc/issues/241) (grilling, autopilot; incumbent evidence cited from #238's H10 = 2 and the tour's dead `extraction` target, not re-run — the surface is replaced): first-run help survives as the **Invoices queue's first-use empty state**, not a tour or overlay (Vic §4b: overlays broke the page, no first-run state exists in Vic); the **empty queue is three states read from data** — first use (never held a document: *No invoices yet* + one lifecycle sentence + **Add invoices** per #243 + the inbound address with Copy, or a link to turn email intake on), done (#239's *Nothing needs you…*), filtered empty (Clear filters) — nothing stored, nothing to dismiss, it ends with the first row; phone gets the same text with the address as its action or *Add invoices from a computer.*; the account menu's Reset tour becomes **How DocuBite works** (small dialog, no spotlight) beside Keyboard shortcuts; no illustration, emerald primary, existing type scale. Glossary: Empty queue. Execution: [#264](https://github.com/petrose99/Wes-doc/issues/264) (blocked by #243); owner sign-off to unplug the tour, Getting-started checklist and Reset tour: [#263](https://github.com/petrose99/Wes-doc/issues/263).

## Not yet specified

- The document-type chooser ("What type of document is this?") on a typed queue's Details tab: a shared review form that predates typed destinations (critique 2026-09-15 Q3, #234). Whether a typed queue still asks, or the type is the destination, sharpens when the Configuration field table (#252) decides what the Details tab shows.
- Facet-panel parity across queues beyond Invoices (PO's Buyer, Receipts' Claim): sharpens per surface as each queue ticket resolves. Bill Pay's Open/Closed sub-states are settled on #229 and built on #251.
- A payments approval flow (who may approve a batch beyond "any owner", amount thresholds, a second signature) and a payments role for members: chartable once Approval Flows (#253) and Users (#254) ship; until then #229's member-submits / owner-decides rule stands.
- SEPA (pain.001) and other payment-file formats beside the ZA EFT CSV, and per-payer-account format defaults: on operator demand; the Payer account model from #229 is where the format would hang.
- Whether Finance folds into Payments (connection state + Open ledger beside the batches) once #248 shrinks it.
- A separate unit-price tolerance setting, Buyer on Purchase Orders, per-line Received (GRN lines), and a manual Close PO: each is data or a control DocuBite lacks today; #228 chose the match-variance percent, no Buyer, no Received, derived Fully invoiced. Revisit only on operator demand or once Admin › PO Mismatch Flows (#253) ships.
- Three-state confidence underline (green / yellow / grey in Vic's PO view) versus #221's two states — revisit only on operator feedback.
- Attachments: Vic's non-invoice document area — whether it needs a home once #245 settles Archive.
- "Is the bank reconciled?" is answered twice, on Health Checks and on Close; #231 kept both where they are (secondary rail), so ownership sharpens with Finance's shape (#248), not with Admin.

## Out of scope

- Reporting and analytics (headline KPIs, spend by category, vendor spend): removed from the app by #237; no operator on the tour needed a chart to work a queue. Returns as its own effort with trustworthy numbers.
- Worksheets, Expenses, Dictation as product features: unplugged by #237 at the owner's call; reviving any of them is a fresh decision, not a resumption.
- Moving money: bank transfers, payment rails, banking providers. Payment runs end at an exported file.
- Vic's visual skin: dark top bar, blue View column, Vic's palette and type.
- A native mobile app. Mobile is responsive web, approval only (#189).
- Marketing surfaces (maps #157, #142).
- Re-deciding #177's closed decisions; they are cited as baseline.

Decide the flagged Dashboard's fate at 20/40: retire it now, or bring it to the bar — and whether its ranked next-best-action moves to the Invoices home

OPEN
## Question

The incumbent Dashboard was critiqued on #238 as the before-baseline and scored **20/40** ([snapshot](https://github.com/petrose99/Wes-doc/blob/codex/post-login-ux-implementation/.impeccable/critique/2026-09-15T20-28-33Z__app-app-workspaces-workspaceid-page-tsx.md)): three P1s — money that contradicts itself on one screen ("ZAR 7,980 outstanding" beside "Total outstanding ZAR 0"), two-thirds of the page empty or redundant chrome, two panel systems on one surface — plus a review list whose rows are indistinguishable and an H1 that says nothing. #237 kept the page reachable for one release behind `DASHBOARD_LANDING`; under the "scores are the work list" rule a page below the bar does not ship, flag or no flag.

Two decisions:

1. **The flagged page.** Retire it now (delete `dashboard/page.tsx` and the flag — a removal, owner signs off by name) or bring it to the bar for its one release (the P1 fixes: one source of truth per number, render analytics only with data, one panel token). Recommendation to argue against: retire — nobody on the tour needed it, and #237 already decided the queue is the home.
2. **The idea worth keeping.** The critique's one authored element was the ranked next-best-action (review > placement > recovery, one CTA, a real "all caught up" state). The Invoices home currently answers "what needs me first" with rail badges and the queue's own sort. Does the ranking survive as something on the queue (a default view, a header line, the empty state), go to #239's journey map, or is the rail sufficient? Aging already went to #229.

Intent: `organize` (does a ranked signal belong on the queue home) then `journey`. Impeccable: `distill` for decision 1, `shape` if decision 2 lands on the queue.

Map: Make the operator app work like Vic.ai (grammar, not skin)
## Destination

DocuBite's authenticated app works the way Vic.ai's does, end to end: **Vic's interaction grammar, DocuBite's skin.** Every operator surface — Invoices, Purchase Orders, Receipts, Bank Statements, Exceptions, Approvals (Invoices / PO Mismatches), Bill Pay, Payment Batches, and Admin — shares one shell: a full-width 62px queue, one header band (View · Sort · summary filter chips opening a hierarchical facet panel), a bulk action row, and one right-hand Detail pane with a sticky bottom action bar. PO mismatches are resolved on the invoice row with per-cell match glyphs and the tolerance arithmetic in view. Payment runs are batched, approved and exported without DocuBite moving money. Admin is a distinct area (Configuration, Approval Flows, Mismatch Flows, Users, Companies) with multi-company access. Approval works on a phone. Implemented and shipped, measured by Impeccable's in-page detector and a critique score above the 20/40 baseline on every queue.

Evidence: the full self-guided tour walked 2026-09-15 — `docs/vic-ai-ux-tour-findings.md` §6 and the screenshots in `docs/vic-ai-tour-2026-09-15/` (DocuBite's own Invoices screen from the same day sits beside them).

## Notes

**Supersedes [Map: Vic.ai-style typed AP surfaces (#177)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/177).** #177's thirty closed decisions are this map's baseline and are cited, not re-decided. Its two open tickets, [Build the five-state processing glyph (#223)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/223) and [Build the typed list-screen composition on all five queues (#225)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/225), are re-parented here. #177 is closed.

**Why a second map.** #177 reached its destination as feature slices bolted onto the old pages, with no ticket owning composition and no in-browser verification, and scored 20/40 ([#224](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/224)). This map charts by *surface*, each ticket owning a whole screen's shape, and every execution ticket closes on detector counts.

**Execution mode.** This map carries execution. Decision tickets resolve first; each spawns an execution ticket; execution tickets close only with `impeccable` run at the four points in CLAUDE.md, in-page detector before/after counts at 1440 and 390 (list and pane-open), and `polish`. Dev-server + seed + headless-Chromium recipe is on #225.

**Design protocol.** Every rendered-surface ticket calls the Skill tool for `impeccable` (sub-command named on the ticket) and `intent`, before the work. Grilling tickets on a surface open with `impeccable critique` of the incumbent and cite the tour screenshot they are matching.

**Vic wins ties, with the tour as the record.** "Does this follow Vic or DocuBite?" defaults to Vic without asking, and the answer is read off `docs/vic-ai-ux-tour-findings.md` §6 and the screenshots — not from memory of the older sections. Grill only what the tour does not settle: DocuBite-only features (Exceptions, Touchless, does-not-move-money, bank statements, institutions), data DocuBite lacks (payment terms, discounts, buyers, entities), and anything that would reverse a #177 decision.

**Documented exceptions to Vic** (decided, do not re-open by "Vic wins ties"): the combined fields+source Detail pane (#179 → #224) with History as its tabs instead of Vic's left panel; the collapsible icon rail instead of Vic's top bar (#224 Q5); DocuBite's palette, type and emerald brand (this map, Q2); Exceptions as its own destination (#192); Touchless keeps its name.

**Settled while charting (grilled 2026-09-15):**

- **Scope is the whole operator app** — queues + Detail pane, Approvals inbox, PO matching in the row, Bill Pay + Payment Batches, Admin, mobile approval. One grammar everywhere.
- **Fidelity is grammar, not skin.** Same layouts, panels, chips, bars, keyboard flow, copy patterns; colour and type stay DocuBite's.
- **Payments never move money.** Bill Pay queue (open bills, terms, countdown, discounted amount over struck-through due) and Payment Batches queue (batch → approve → export file). The transfer stays outside DocuBite, as `preparePaymentRun` does today.
- **Approvals is a destination with two queues**, Invoices and PO Mismatches, each a personal Ready-to-Approve view with the sticky Approve/Reject bar. Exceptions stays separate.
- **Admin adopts Vic's full IA including Companies**: Configuration (per-field Editable/Required/Width, consequence toggles), Approval Flows, PO Mismatch Flows, Users, Companies — one login, many companies, per-entity permissions. This is the one schema-and-auth effort on the map; it is researched before it is grilled.
- **Build order:** shell (#225) → distill (#238) → Approvals → PO matching → Payments → Admin → Mobile.
- **Removal protocol (owner's rule, #237):** nothing is removed from the app without the owner signing off each removal by name on the ticket. Removed features are *unplugged* (CONTEXT.md term), not deleted, so a return is a re-link.

- A native mobile app. Mobile is responsive web, approval only (#189).
- Marketing surfaces (maps #157, #142).

## Resolution (grilled 2026-09-15, two rounds, owner signed off every removal)

**Principle:** a working person's day is "what needs me, in what order, am I done." Vic answers it with the queue as the home; the Dashboard answered it a second time with nine blocks (Intent: Inconsistent Patterns / Assumption of Context, Category 9). Distill removes the second answer.

1. **Landing screen = the Invoices queue**, desktop and mobile. No overview surface. Old Dashboard reachable at `/dashboard` behind a `DASHBOARD_LANDING` flag for one release.
2. **Dashboard blocks:** drop Welcome+Upload, Next best action + chips, stat cards, Recent files, Needs your review. Open invoices by age → input to #229 (Bill Pay KPI). Headline KPIs + both charts → removed, reporting **out of scope** on this map (returns as its own effort).

5:Vic.ai markets itself as an "Autonomous Finance Platform — Accountable AI for Accounts Payable." The demo covers: Admin View, Autonomous Invoice Processing, Approvals, Autonomous PO Matching, and Payments. 16:- Every list screen has the same three-part header: **View switcher → Sort → Filters** (filter chips shown inline, e.g. "Status: Open Invoices", "Invoice Approval: 4 Approved or Not Started..."), so the mental model of "which subset am I looking at" is always visible, not hidden in a slide-over.
26:Two-column "per entity" rollups: **Open Invoices Per Entity**, **Pending Approvals Per Entity**, **Pending PO Mismatch Approvals Per Entity** — plain tables of entity name → count, each entity name a link. No charts, no color. It's a triage list, not a BI dashboard, and it's honest about that (one panel says "There are currently no PO mismatches for you to review" as a plain empty state, not a graphic).
36:- Clicking a user opens a right panel with **Information / Companies** tabs; under Companies, permissions are scoped **per entity** (User Type: Accountant/Approver radio, User Level checkboxes) rather than one global role. Each entity the user has access to gets its own expandable section with its own role settings and its own remove (✕) button.
38:**Takeaway**: DocuBite likely only needs this if multi-entity/multi-company access is a real use case — otherwise this is over-engineering to copy wholesale. Worth adopting only the *idea* (permissions are entity-scoped, not just role-scoped) if DocuBite ever supports multiple companies per account.
43:[Omitted long matching line]
44:- **Audit tab** (in the same right panel, next to a per-invoice "Approval" tab): a chronological activity log — "Gavin — demogavin@vic.ai — Uploaded invoice — 2/16/2023 | 12:47 PM" — with a manual "Refresh audit log" action.
45:- **Approval tab**: shows the approval chain as **named steps** ("STEP 1 — Rejected", "One user must approve this step"), each step listing the specific approver(s) by name/email, a rejection reason typed by the rejecting user ("duplicate"), and a full initiated-by/timestamp trail at the bottom. This is a real audit trail with human accountability baked in, not just a status enum.
49:- PO-backed invoices get a small PDF-shaped icon; a **red badge with a number** (e.g. a red "1" superscript) on the icon signals "N mismatches to resolve" without opening the row.
50:- The "Purchase Orders" column shows the matched PO number as an inline **editable/removable chip** (with an "×" or count badge for multiple candidate POs on one invoice).
56:- The right pane in PO matching shows the **actual source invoice PDF** with the matched PO number, dates, and line items highlighted/boxed directly on the document image — reinforcing the same "structured data next to literal source" pairing as invoice review.
65:This section completes the walkthrough of the "Approvals" and "Payments" guided tours (previously only summarized), including their mobile counterparts, plus what was found for Attachments.
70:- Once submitted, the approver's own view becomes a **personal "Ready to Approve" inbox** (View • Default = "Ready to Approve"), scoped to invoices assigned to them — this is a distinct saved view, not a filter the user has to build.
71:- Approving/rejecting from this inbox opens an **"Approve Invoices" modal**: an optional free-text **Comment** field, an **"Eligible for Approval (N of M)" status strip** (green dot) showing how many of the selected items actually qualify, a recap table (Type/Vendor/Invoice Number/Amount), and a single confiral button labelled with the exact count — **"Approve Invoices (1)"**. Bulk approval never hides the count behind a generic "Confirm."
75:- **Home screen ("Welcome Back!")**: two large tappable summary cards — "Awaiting Your Approvals: 1 Invoice → Go to Approvals" and "No PO Mismatches → Go to PO Mismatch Approvals." Even with zero items in one queue, the empty queue still gets its own card and CTA (consistent presence, not a hidden empty state).
76:- **List screen ("Ready to Approve")**: each row is a card, not a table row — due date, a status pill ("In Progress"), amount in green, vendor name. Card-based density on mobile vs. table density on desktop — the same data, re-composed per surface rather than a squeezed-down table.

83:- **Bill Pay list** columns: Vendor, Invoice Number, Invoice Date, **Terms** (e.g. "2-10-30" shown in purple/blue), Due Date, a **due/discount countdown badge**, Bill Total, Currency, Est. Arrival Date (payment method icon + date), **Amount To Pay** (editable, defaults to the discounted amount when eligible), **Pay From** (bank account, editable per row).
84:- **Two distinct countdown badge colors carry two different meanings**: a **purple lightning-bolt badge "⚡ Expires in N Days"** means an early-payment cash discount is about to lapse (urgency = money left on the table); a plain **blue "N Days Away"** badge is just the standard due-date countdown with no discount at stake. 7:**Workspace home**:
8-The Invoices queue. Opening a workspace lands the user on their work, not on a summary of it; "what needs me" is read from the rail badges and the queue's own counts. There is no separate overview surface.

11:**Unplugged surface**:
12-A feature the product no longer shows or routes to, kept only so it can be brought back deliberately. Worksheets, Expenses and Dictation are unplugged. An unplugged surface has no navigation entry, no row or bulk action, no badge, and its addresses do not open.
13-_Avoid_: Hidden, deprecated, legacy
14-
15-**Core workflow destinations**:
16-Invoices, Purchase Orders, Receipts, Bank Statements, Exceptions, Finance, and Archive: the permission-filtered peer surfaces representing typed intake, escalated work, booked outcome, and the permanent source record. The four typed intake destinations replace the former single "Documents" surface.

69-The personal system view on the Approvals destination: every Approval whose current stage the signed-in person can decide, including rows that are not yet eligible, shown with the reason. The badge on the rail counts this view and nothing else.

72-**Send back for review**:
73-The reversible middle path on an Approval: the stage is not decided, the invoice returns to review with a required reason, and the run can be restarted. Reject ends the run.

Base directory for this skill: /home/ubuntu/Dev/Wes-doc/.claude/skills/grilling

Interview the user relentlessly until you reach a shared understanding. Map this as a **design tree**: every decision branches into the decisions that hang off it.

Work the tree in **rounds**. The **frontier** is every decision whose prerequisites are already settled: the questions you can ask _now_ without guessing at answers you haven't heard yet. Ask the whole frontier in one round: number each question and give your recommended answer. Then wait for the user's answers before the next round.

Format a round like so:

```
❓ **Q1** - **<question title>**: <question body, might be multiple paragraphs, including multiple choices>

➡️ <your recommended answer>

---

❓ **Q2** - **<question title>**: <question body, might be multiple paragraphs, including multiple choices>

➡️ <your recommended answer>
```

Each round the user answers reshapes the tree: settled decisions push the frontier outward and unblock questions that depended on them. Recompute the frontier and ask the next round. A question whose answer depends on another question still open in this round belongs to a _later_ round, not this one.

Finding _facts_ is your job, never the user's. When a frontier question needs a fact from the environment (filesystem, tools, etc.), dispatch a sub-agent to find it; don't ask the user for anything you could look up yourself. Don't block on it: a running exploration is an unsettled prerequisite, so only the questions downstream of it wait for the sub-agent to report; ask the rest of the frontier now. The _decisions_ are the user's: put each to them and wait.

The session is done when the frontier is empty: every branch of the design tree visited, nothing left silently assumed. Do not act on it until the user confirms you have reached a shared understanding.

Base directory for this skill: /home/ubuntu/Dev/Wes-doc/.claude/skills/domain-modeling

# Domain Modeling

Actively build and sharpen the project's domain model as you design. This is the *active* discipline: challenging terms, inventing edge-case scenarios, and writing the glossary and decisions down the moment they crystallise. (Merely *reading* `CONTEXT.md` for vocabulary is not this skill: that's a one-line habit any skill can do. This skill is for when you're changing the model, not just consuming it.)

## File structure

Most repos have a single context:

```
/
├── CONTEXT.md
├── docs/
│   └── adr/
│       ├── 0001-event-sourced-orders.md
│       └── 0002-postgres-for-write-model.md
└── src/
```

If a `CONTEXT-MAP.md` exists at the root, the repo has multiple contexts. The map points to where each one lives:

```
/
├── CONTEXT-MAP.md
├── docs/
│   └── adr/                          ← system-wide decisions
├── src/
│   ├── ordering/
│   │   ├── CONTEXT.md
│   │   └── docs/adr/                 ← context-specific decisions
│   └── billing/
│       ├── CONTEXT.md
│       └── docs/adr/
```

Create files lazily: only when you have something to write. If no `CONTEXT.md` exists, create one when the first term is resolved. If no `docs/adr/` exists, create it when the first ADR is needed.

## During the session

### Challenge against the glossary

When the user uses a term that conflicts with the existing language in `CONTEXT.md`, call it out immediately. "Your glossary defines 'cancellation' as X, but you seem to mean Y. Which is it?"

### Sharpen fuzzy language

When the user uses vague or overloaded terms, propose a precise canonical term. "You're saying 'account': do you mean the Customer or the User? Those are different things."

### Discuss concrete scenarios

When domain relationships are being discussed, stress-test them with specific scenarios. Invent scenarios that probe edge cases and force the user to be precise about the boundaries between concepts.

### Cross-reference with code

When the user states how something works, check whether the code agrees. If you find a contradiction, surface it: "Your code cancels entire Orders, but you just said partial cancellation is possible. Which is right?"

### Update CONTEXT.md inline

When a term is resolved, update `CONTEXT.md` right there. Don't batch these up: capture them as they happen. Use the format in [CONTEXT-FORMAT.md](./CONTEXT-FORMAT.md).

`CONTEXT.md` should be totally devoid of implementation details. Do not treat `CONTEXT.md` as a spec, a scratch pad, or a repository for implementation decisions. It is a glossary and nothing else.

### Offer ADRs sparingly

Only offer to create an ADR when all three are true:

1. **Hard to reverse**: the cost of changing your mind later is meaningful
2. **Surprising without context**: a future reader will wonder "why did they do it this way?"
3. **The result of a real trade-off**: there were genuine alternatives and you picked one for specific reasons

If any of the three is missing, skip the ADR. Use the format in [ADR-FORMAT.md](./ADR-FORMAT.md).
